carmen: Quick thread — I ran a small sweep comparing streaming (SSE chunked) vs non-streaming (websocket/full-response) for redwood-3b-q8 across GPUs/regions. TL;DR numbers below, want sizing guidance and any kernel/infra notes.

jia: Nice, can you include p50/p95 and tokens/sec and the batching config you used?

carmen: Batch=auto (continuous batching), max_tokens=1024, prompt ~128 tokens. Streaming configured to flush chunks every 32 tokens. Each datapoint is a single-GPU run, steady-state synthetic traffic (50 concurrent clients) for 5m.

matt: Results? :eyes:

carmen: Paste of raw summary (human-readable):

```
us-west1 (A100-80GB):
  SSE streaming   -> p50 42ms,  p95 160ms, tokens/sec 820
  WS non-stream   -> p50 28ms,  p95 320ms, tokens/sec 1250

eu-west1 (H100):
  SSE streaming   -> p50 25ms,  p95 110ms, tokens/sec 1700
  WS non-stream   -> p50 18ms,  p95 210ms, tokens/sec 2100

asia-east1 (A100-40GB):
  SSE streaming   -> p50 60ms,  p95 240ms, tokens/sec 640
  WS non-stream   -> p50 40ms,  p95 420ms, tokens/sec 980
```

carmen: Notes: H100 shows much better streaming tokens/sec (flash attention + fused KV paths). A100-40GB in APAC hit memory/fragmentation which hurts SSE (more frequent KV flushes). WS non-streaming tends to get higher raw tokens/sec but sometimes worse p95 (esp. us-west A100 p95 320ms) due to longer collect/finalization path.

olivia: Interesting that WS p95 can be higher than SSE on A100. Might be request coalescing + large tail due to queuing. Did you measure percent of requests that hit fallback (CPU) kernel?

carmen: Checked logs — negligible CPU fallbacks. More likely batching spikes: WS burst at end causes larger final batches and slightly longer tails. Streaming evens out latency but costs some throughput on older kernels.

jia: For capacity sizing, recommend using this formula:
```
needed_gpus = ceil((expected_tokens_per_sec) / (tokens_per_sec_per_gpu))
```
Example: if product needs 100k tokens/sec in eu-west1 and H100 gives 1700 tps per GPU (SSE) -> ~59 GPUs. Add 15% headroom for burst + rolling upgrades.

matt: Kernel detail request: which attention/kernel stack used? cuBLAS GEMM path or flash/fused path?

carmen: H100 runs on fused flash-attn variant + optimized KV kernels. A100-80GB ran mixed: cutlass + attention fusion for core, A100-40GB fell back to less-fused due to memory layout, which explains lower streaming throughput.

perf-bot: perf-run-complete: id=run-1779001220 status=ok artifacts:/runs/1779001220/results.csv

olivia: Good call on headroom. Also consider region-specific autoscale thresholds — APAC should have more conservative concurrency limits for SSE.

carmen: TL;DR actionable:
- Use WS (non-stream) for max raw throughput-oriented endpoints (batching-friendly workloads).
- Use SSE streaming for interactive workloads where consistent p50 is prioritized, but watch p95 on older GPUs/APAC.
- Prefer H100 or kernels with fused flash-attn for streaming-heavy traffic.
- Sizing formula above + +15% headroom.

carmen: I'll follow up with a small spreadsheet and invite infra/product to sizing sync. Anyone want the raw traces?

jia: Yes please, include traces + the per-request batch sizes. Thanks!

matt: +1, want to validate with multi-GPU runs (cross-GPU KV sharing).

carmen: Adding multi-GPU scaling to the list. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
